title: KKR release Rahane and Pathirana, keep Rs 41.65 crore for auction as Dhoni becomes CSK mentor
dek: All ten IPL franchises have named the players they are keeping for 2027. Lucknow have the biggest purse, Gujarat the smallest, and MS Dhoni has ended his playing career after 19 seasons.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Kolkata Knight Riders have released their captain of the last two seasons, Ajinkya Rahane, and the Sri Lankan fast bowler Matheesha Pathirana, their most expensive release, and will go into the IPL 2027 auction with Rs 41.65 crore to spend, the second-largest purse of the ten teams, according to the lists published after Tuesday's retention deadline. MS Dhoni has ended his IPL playing career and will be Chennai Super Kings' team mentor next season, the league said.

Lucknow Super Giants have the most money left, Rs 47.45 crore, and Gujarat Titans the least, Rs 8.75 crore, according to reports. The auction is due to be held on 16 December, according to reports; the BCCI has not yet formally announced the date or venue.

## Kolkata's squad

KKR have retained 17 players, including the Australian all-rounder Cameron Green, Sunil Narine, Varun Chakaravarthy, Rinku Singh, Harshit Rana, Angkrish Raghuvanshi and Anukul Roy, according to one team-by-team list; another report gave a shorter list of 14, so the final count should be checked against the franchise's own announcement. They have eight places to fill, three of them for overseas players.

Apart from Rahane and Pathirana, KKR let go of Bangladesh's Mustafizur Rahman, New Zealand's Rachin Ravindra, Zimbabwe's Blessing Muzarabani, and the Indian players Rahul Tripathi, Akash Deep, Navdeep Saini and Umran Malik, according to reports. Releasing Rahane means KKR will need a new captain; they have not named one.

## Dhoni moves off the field

Dhoni played 19 IPL seasons, 17 of them for Chennai and two for Rising Pune Supergiant, and scored 5,439 runs in 278 matches at an average of 38.30 and a strike rate of 137.45, the IPL said in a tribute on its website. His 201 dismissals as wicketkeeper are the most in the league, and he led Chennai to five titles, in 2010, 2011, 2018, 2021 and 2023, joint-most with Rohit Sharma. He handed the captaincy to Ruturaj Gaikwad in 2024.

## The other nine teams

The biggest names released include Australia's Travis Head and Mitchell Starc, who had been with Sunrisers Hyderabad and Delhi Capitals respectively, and New Zealand's Trent Boult from Mumbai Indians, according to reports. Delhi also released Karun Nair and Bengal's Abishek Porel, who scored a fifty for Bengal against Chandigarh in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy on Monday. Lucknow released Avesh Khan, Anrich Nortje and Wanindu Hasaranga, and Rajasthan Royals released Shimron Hetmyer.

Several big moves had already been made through trades announced by the league before the deadline: Hardik Pandya has moved from Mumbai to Punjab Kings and Arshdeep Singh from Punjab to Mumbai; Mohammed Shami has joined Rajasthan; Sam Curran has gone to Lucknow; and Harshal Patel has moved from Hyderabad to Gujarat.

Remaining purses, according to reports:

- Lucknow Super Giants: Rs 47.45 crore (7 places, 3 overseas)
- Kolkata Knight Riders: Rs 41.65 crore (8 places, 3 overseas)
- Sunrisers Hyderabad: Rs 40.15 crore (7 places, 3 overseas)
- Delhi Capitals: Rs 39.50 crore (9 places, 4 overseas)
- Mumbai Indians: Rs 32.60 crore (9 places, 2 overseas)
- Chennai Super Kings: Rs 28.05 crore (6 places, 2 overseas)
- Rajasthan Royals: Rs 27.05 crore (6 places, 3 overseas)
- Punjab Kings: Rs 18.60 crore (6 places, 2 overseas)
- Royal Challengers Bengaluru: Rs 14.15 crore (5 places, 1 overseas)
- Gujarat Titans: Rs 8.75 crore (3 places, 2 overseas)

## What happens next

The 2027 auction is expected to be the last mini-auction of the current cycle, with a full mega auction before the 2028 season, according to reports. India's Test players, meanwhile, begin the first Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington at 3.30 am IST on Thursday.
